purpose: Measure what actually contains an arbitrary-code effect at the Wolfram evaluator on this machine, to decide WolframGuard's ReadOnly enforcement. State measured independently (Python sqlite/os), not trusted from the kernel's own return values.

scenario_A_StartProtectedMode.mechanism: Developer`StartProtectedMode["Read"->{task}, "Write"->{scratch}, "Execute"->{}, "ResolveAllowedPaths"->False] in the evaluator kernel (the same primitive AgentTools' own Local method uses)
scenario_A_StartProtectedMode.jdbc_SQLExecute_DELETE_via_warm_connecti: NOT CONTAINED - returned 250, DB inactive 250 -> 0. The JVM/JDBC driver writes the SQLite file directly, outside Wolfram's ProtectedMode file guard.
scenario_A_StartProtectedMode.EndProtectedMode_escape_attempt: INERT - Developer`EndProtectedMode[] returned unevaluated; a post-'end' DeleteFile was still blocked. Untrusted code cannot turn protection off.
scenario_A_StartProtectedMode.conclusion: A Wolfram-level sandbox contains WL filesystem/process effects and cannot be escaped from inside, but does NOT contain JDBC/Java database writes.

scenario_B_OS_readonly_ACL.mechanism: icacls /deny <user>:(OI)(CI)(WD,AD,DC,DE,WA,WEA) on the task directory; no WL sandbox
scenario_B_OS_readonly_ACL.conclusion: An OS deny-write lock contains BOTH WL and JDBC writes - language-agnostic, because the OS refuses the write regardless of which primitive or runtime issues it.

legit_read_under_lock: Under the same deny-write lock, a legitimate SELECT COUNT(... 'inactive') via JDBC returns {{250}} while a DELETE on the same connection fails (WRITE-FAILED), DB stays 250. Reads pass, writes do not, so ReadOnly does not break legitimate read-only tasks.
design_decision: WolframGuard ReadOnly rests on the OS deny-write lock (primary enforcement; contains JDBC and any write primitive) plus $AllowInternet=False (network). The effect classifier is demoted to a pre-filter that rejects obvious danger early and blocks the process/network axes so the lock cannot be tampered with by spawning a tool. StartProtectedMode is the validated in-kernel complement but is insufficient alone for JDBC, so the OS lock is what the read-only guarantee rests on. Proven by the ContainmentOnly policy (classifier disabled) in results/wolframguard-containment-001.
reproduce: probe_containment.py (copied into this directory); measures A and B against fresh fixtures.
